children: Digital advertising technology company Perion Network

has agreed to be acquired by Affle in an all-cash transaction valued at approximately $420 million, expanding Affle’s presence in connected television, retail media and other digital advertising channels.

Under the agreement announced Sunday, Perion shareholders will receive $11.70 a share, representing a 34.5% premium to the stock’s closing price on Oct. 30. Perion’s board unanimously approved the transaction, which is expected to close in early 2027, subject to shareholder approval, regulatory clearance and other customary conditions.
For investors, the agreement offers Perion

shareholders a substantial premium and a defined cash exit, although the deal remains subject to closing risks. The transaction also highlights continued consolidation in advertising technology as companies seek to combine capabilities across mobile, connected television and other digital platforms. Perion’s $228.3 million in cash, short-term deposits and marketable securities as of Sept. 30 represents more than half the proposed equity purchase price.

Affle, which specializes in mobile advertising and consumer acquisition technology, plans to integrate Perion’s capabilities in retail media, connected television, digital out-of-home advertising and other channels. The combination would broaden Affle’s advertising offerings while potentially creating opportunities to cross-sell services to advertisers and publishers.

Perion Chief Executive Tal Jacobson said the companies’ technologies and geographic reach could complement each other, while Affle CEO Anuj Khanna Sohum identified opportunities to expand the combined business in sectors including e-commerce, retail and healthcare. Perion will retain its brand and operate as a wholly owned Affle subsidiary following the acquisition.

The agreement includes a 40-day period during which Perion can solicit competing acquisition proposals. That window expires Dec. 11, potentially allowing another bidder to offer shareholders a higher price. However, the company cautioned that no alternative transaction is assured.

Citibank is providing debt financing for the acquisition, which isn't contingent on financing arrangements. If completed, the transaction will end Perion’s public listing on Nasdaq and the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange.

title: Affle to acquire Perion for $420M in all-cash deal
